subject.title: [Bug]: Unscheduled reminder guard fires for isolated-session crons + counter lost during compaction

question: Should maintainers adopt or refresh the open fork PR that closes this issue, or create a narrow target-repo replacement for the same two-part fix?
rationale: The bug is source-proven and the fix boundary is clear, but an exact closing fork PR exists in a conflicting state and a same-repo PR covers only one variant, so maintainers should choose the landing path before automation creates duplicate work.

options.title: Adopt Or Replace Focused Fix
options.body: Use the fork PR as source material or open a narrow target-repo replacement that fixes both isolated-cron matching and compaction-counter preservation with regression coverage.

options.title: Wait On Fork PR
options.body: Keep this issue paired with the fork PR and wait for the contributor to refresh it into a mergeable target-repo path.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Reminder Work
options.body: Defer this exact bug behind broader reminder-guard cleanup, accepting that the isolated-cron false positive remains open meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Adopt Or Replace Focused Fix
recommendation.body: Use the fork PR as source material or open a narrow target-repo replacement that fixes both isolated-cron matching and compaction-counter preservation with regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing owner from recent guard and embedded-agent runtime history, and can choose whether to adopt, replace, or fold the fix into broader reminder work.
